extracted.intended_audience: artists, creators, independent inventors seeking patent help and volunteer patent attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for inventors (particularly artists/creators) seeking pro bono help drafting design or utility patent applications and for attorneys who want to volunteer with the VLA Patent Pro Bono Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible participants (target audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists, creators, and independent inventors who are interested in applying for a design patent or a utility patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's main goal is to provide application drafting services for those who have not yet filed an application for a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing-stage requirement / exception policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The main goal is to provide application drafting services for those who have not yet filed an application for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who have already filed a provisional application, or have filed a non‑provisional application and have received a USPTO office action, may be admitted on a case‑by‑case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — Intake form / registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors must fill out an intake form (preferred) or email the program to register interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact method: use the intake form (preferred) or email [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — Qualification questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial registration, VLA will send a questionnaire to see if you qualify to participate in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing and returning the questionnaire is required for the program to assess eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Attorney review and follow‑up
rubrics_metrics.description: Once VLA receives your completed questionnaire, it will be reviewed by an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often, the reviewing attorney will have substantive follow‑up questions. This intake process can take several weeks to several months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 — Screening consultation and membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an attorney recommends that your case move forward, VLA will schedule a screening consultation with an attorney. During the consultation, you will receive preliminary advice on how to protect your invention before filing your patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to booking a consultation, a VLA membership fee is due (further details provided by VLA). Discounts are available for full‑time students. Financially‑eligible inventors over the age of 60 are entitled to a free VLA membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 — Pro bono placement policy for financially‑eligible matters
rubrics_metrics.description: For financially‑eligible inventors, matters ready for pro bono representation are circulated within VLA's network of volunteer attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A volunteer patent attorney will contact you should they decide to take on your case. While placement rates are high, placement cannot be guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer attorney requirements — orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: To volunteer for a case, attorneys are required to attend an hour‑long orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the orientation you will learn important information about the programs, volunteer requirements, and administrative procedures. Registration link provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary resources and USPTO links
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides links to additional inventor resources such as The Inventor’s Patent Academy and various USPTO resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource links include: The Inventor’s Patent Academy (learn.inventtogether.org), USPTO Subscription Center (content.govdelivery.com), USPTO Free Resources (uspto.gov/free-services), and USPTO Inventor and Entrepreneur Resources (uspto.gov/inventors).
